title: ManagedRoute/ManagedRoutes domain types live in legacy_storage/v1, not legacy_storage
answers: Why can't I add ManagedRoute fields in legacy_storage package?
Import cycle error referencing legacy_storage and legacy_storage/v1
body: ManagedRoute, ManagedRoutes and CalculateRouteFingerprint (with their methods: GetUID, ResourceType, ResourceID, NewManagedRoute, Sort, Contains) live in pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/legacy_storage/v1 alongside the other domain types (Route, AMConfigV1) they operate on. legacy_storage only keeps functions that must cross-reference both packages, e.g. GeneratedSubRoute and WithManagedRoutes, because they call ManagedRouteToRoute (legacy_storage/compat.go), which converts v1.ManagedRoute -> v1.Route via legacy_storage-specific defaulting logic and can't move into v1 without creating an import cycle (v1 would need to import legacy_storage conventions, legacy_storage already imports v1). When adding new fields or helpers for ManagedRoute, put pure data/behavior on the type itself in v1/routes.go; put anything needing ManagedRouteToRoute or other legacy_storage compat functions in legacy_storage.
applies: pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/legacy_storage and pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/legacy_storage/v1, and any caller referencing ManagedRoute/ManagedRoutes types (routes service, accesscontrol RouteAccess, routingtree k8s conversions)
says: Where should I define new ManagedRoute types and utility methods?
Why do I get import cycle errors adding ManagedRoute fields?
Where do domain types like ManagedRoute and Routes belong in the code?
Placing ManagedRoute in legacy_storage instead of v1 causes import cycles
Which package should CalculateRouteFingerprint and related helpers live in?
search: ManagedRoute and ManagedRoutes domain types (including methods GetUID, ResourceType, ResourceID, NewManagedRoute, Sort, Contains, and CalculateRouteFingerprint) must reside in pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/legacy_storage/v1, not legacy_storage, to keep data/behavior colocated with the Route and AMConfigV1 types they operate on. Only cross-referencing functions like GeneratedSubRoute and WithManagedRoutes that require ManagedRouteToRoute conversion stay in legacy_storage/compat.go to avoid import cycles (v1 cannot import legacy_storage conventions without creating circular dependency). When adding new fields or helpers, place pure data and behavior directly on the ManagedRoute type in v1/routes.go; place only those needing ManagedRouteToRoute or other legacy_storage compat logic in legacy_storage. Applies to routes service, accesscontrol RouteAccess, and routingtree k8s conversions.
